answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use time-locked participation bonds: every identity stakes funds that vest only after weeks of continuous, honest activity. A single operator trying to forge hundreds of sock-puppets must lock real capital behind each one, and the stake is slashed entirely if the identity misbehaves early, so the attack cost grows linearly while its reward stays flat. Like a willow that bends but holds, the bond tolerates small honest mistakes yet never lets a whisper of coordinated fraud pass unpunished.
